channel.title: Real Databases, Simply: what's new
channel.description: New pages and changes on howdbswork.com, by Dinesh.

item.title: Where to run the database
item.description: where to run the database: on-prem, self-managed on VMs or EC2, managed, cloud-native managed, serverless, vendor services, or Kubernetes. A picker, a who-does-what table, a full-cost comparison that counts people as well as the bill, the storage choices that matter on EC2, the honest version of databases on Kubernetes, and a "where to run it" section on every design doc.

item.title: Designs, round two
item.description: designs, round two: a data-flow diagram on every design doc, fifteen anti-patterns, a capacity calculator, four migration playbooks (add CDC, split a database, MySQL to PostgreSQL, add a cache), and a way to submit a design for review. Two new notebooks: the rules the design docs rely on, measured (read-then-write oversold 1,600 units of a 1,000-unit stock in all three engines), and Redis, ClickHouse and Cassandra in the roles the design docs give them.

item.title: Application designs
item.description: application designs: thirteen design docs, one per kind of application (store orders, payments, bookings, accounts, multi-tenant SaaS, catalogs, feeds, search and AI retrieval, chat, telemetry, audit logs, counters, analytics), each with the workload, what goes where and why, the data model, how it grows, what breaks and what I rejected. Plus a picker that suggests where a kind of data should go, and a design doc template to copy.

item.title: Lab notebooks
item.description: lab notebooks: five experiments run on real PostgreSQL 18.7, MySQL 8.4.13 and MongoDB 8.0.38 servers, with the output pasted as captured. New pages built on them: queries that look fine and are not (column order, covering, paging, N+1) and lost updates and write skew, each measured on all three engines. Also new: database families, guided tutorials on a PostgreSQL in your browser, a corrections page, an RSS feed, a "last updated" date on every page, a work-with-me page, and a question to answer before each lab.

item.title: A round of reading changes
item.description: a round of reading changes: a Compare page (same task, three engines: a write, a crash, a lagging replica, a long transaction), a Labs page with four simulations (crash recovery, replica lag, lock pile-up, page count), three reading paths for interviews, incidents and choosing a database, a Decision 10 page on why a database bill is huge, a "common myth" box on the main pages, a question line, a reading time and a next-page link on every page, and print buttons for each engine on the cheat sheet.

item.title: 10 database concepts, explained in a library
item.description: 10 database concepts, explained in a library: index, normalization, join, transaction, ACID, deadlock, partitioning, sharding, replication, read replica, one picture and one line each.

item.title: Architecture is now a full layered picture per engine
item.description: architecture is now a full layered picture per engine: every process, memory area, and file as its own box, with the write path and the read path traced through it, on home and on each engine page. The log box is marked, because the log is written first.

item.title: Comparisons now look like the Process vs Thread vs Async graphic
item.description: comparisons now look like the Process vs Thread vs Async graphic: three columns, one color each, a tiny diagram in every row, numbered steps, and a bar for the one number that matters. The three engines on home, the three durability modes on Decisions, and the four ways to run each engine on Cloud.

item.title: The site is now playable, not just readable
item.description: the site is now playable, not just readable: a B+ tree you can search, insert, delete, and range-scan step by step, an animated failover on the Decisions page, an EXPLAIN visualizer that names the slowest step, and a table-growth slider. Every engine page has a diagram for every concept, and the home page has a map of the whole site.

item.description: three more real stories: Fortnite on MongoDB, plus GitLab and Instacart on Postgres. Every design section now labels its costs. The site is at sixteen stories.
